questions.stemEn: A picture consistent with amniotic band sequence is provided with no other abnormality. What determines the outcome?

options.text: Time of occurrence affects the degree of anomaly
It is part of an association

questions.explanationAr: في amniotic disruption sequence، نوع وشدة التشوهات يعتمدان على توقيت حدوث disruption أثناء embryonic/fetal development وعلى شدة الحدث. لذلك مفتاح المصدر هو أن timing يحدد degree and pattern of anomaly.
questions.reasoningEn: The source states that the type of structural anomaly depends on the stage of embryonic development and severity of disruption.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: وصف الحالة بأنها association لا يجيب عن العامل الذي يحدد شدة ونوع التشوهات في هذا السؤال.
questions.clinicalPearl: Earlier disruptive events can produce more extensive craniofacial and body-wall defects; later events more often cause constriction or limb defects.

questions.stemEn: A 2-month-old male infant had a head circumference below the fifth percentile at birth and it has increased only 1 cm since birth. Which is the most likely cause?
questions.explanationAr: لأن head circumference كان صغيرًا منذ الولادة، فالمصدر يصنف الحالة congenital microcephaly ويختار first-trimester toxoplasmosis من الخيارات. ويضع perinatal asphyxia وIVH وcraniosynostosis والعدوى المتأخرة ضمن أسباب acquired microcephaly في شرحه.
questions.reasoningEn: The source distinguishes congenital microcephaly present at birth from acquired microcephaly developing after birth.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: وفق شرح المصدر، perinatal asphyxia وIVH والعدوى المتأخرة ترتبط أكثر بـacquired microcephaly. Craniosynostosis قد يحد نمو الرأس لكنه ليس المفتاح المختار في هذا recall.
questions.clinicalPearl: Timing of onset is a major clue when distinguishing congenital from acquired microcephaly.

questions.stemEn: A 4-week-old boy has macrocephaly, split coronal and sagittal sutures by 1 cm, and a bulging fontanelle. Both parents have head circumferences above the 95th percentile. What is the most likely explanation?
questions.explanationAr: رغم وجود macrocephaly عند الوالدين، فإن split sutures + bulging fontanelle هي red flags لraised intracranial pressure؛ لذلك المصدر يختار hydrocephalus وليس familial macrocephaly.
questions.reasoningEn: Bulging fontanelle and suture separation indicate increased intracranial pressure, which points to hydrocephalus in the listed choices.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Familial macrocephaly عادةً لا ترافقها علامات raised ICP. Achondroplasia قد تسبب macrocephaly لكنها لا تفسر هذه العلامات الحادة وحدها.
questions.clinicalPearl: Do not label macrocephaly as familial when signs of raised intracranial pressure are present.

questions.stemEn: A picture of cleft palate is provided. When is the appropriate time for closure?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يذكر أن cleft lip repair يكون أبكر، بينما palatal closure عادةً تُستكمل تقريبًا بين 9 أشهر وسنة، ولذلك اختار 9 months من الخيارات.
questions.reasoningEn: The source cites AAP material stating palatal clefts are usually repaired later than lip clefts, typically around 9 to 12 months.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: 3 months مبكر بالنسبة للـpalate وفق المصدر، و18 months أو2 years متأخران عن التوقيت المذكور في شرحه.
questions.clinicalPearl: Timing of cleft-palate repair balances speech development, feeding, and craniofacial growth and may vary by surgical program.

questions.stemEn: A newborn has microtia with no other congenital anomaly. Which investigation should be performed next?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار Auditory Brainstem Response لأن microtia كثيرًا ما تترافق مع external/middle ear abnormalities وconductive hearing loss، ولذلك hearing assessment يجب أن يتم مبكرًا. المصدر يذكر أيضًا أن renal ultrasound قد يكون موصى به في التقييم، وهذا يجعل السؤال مهمًا للمراجعة من حيث ترتيب الخطوات.
questions.reasoningEn: The recalled key prioritizes early hearing assessment with ABR, while the source discussion also mentions renal screening.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Renal ultrasound ليس خيارًا بلا قيمة؛ بالعكس المصدر يذكره كفحص screening أيضًا، لذلك لا نعتبره خطأ مطلقًا ونبقي السؤال needs_verification. Echocardiography/genetic testing يعتمدان على associated findings.
questions.clinicalPearl: Microtia requires prompt audiologic evaluation; associated-anomaly screening depends on the clinical context and current recommendations.

tts.text: A newborn has microtia with no other congenital anomaly. Which investigation should be performed next? A. Renal ultrasound. B. Echocardiography. C. Auditory brainstem response. D. Genetic study.

questions.stemEn: A picture is provided of an infant with a clenched fist. What should be done next?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر نفسه يضع علامة استفهام على الإجابة ويقول إن لا features إضافية مذكورة. Clenched fist قد يكون clue لchromosomal anomaly، لكن الصورة والسياق ضروريان؛ لذلك نحفظ karyotyping كـrecalledAnswer فقط ولا نثبتها.
questions.reasoningEn: The source tentatively favors karyotyping but explicitly notes that the vignette lacks other features.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: لا يمكن استبعاد Brain MRI أوتحديد الاختبار الأمثل دون معرفة شكل اليد وبقية الفحص السريري.
questions.clinicalPearl: A single dysmorphic sign should be interpreted in the context of the full phenotype before choosing genetic testing.
